subject: chemistry
title: Polymer structure
key_idea: Polymers are made of very large molecules: long chains of atoms joined by strong covalent bonds. The intermolecular forces between the chains are relatively strong, so polymers are solids at room temperature. Cross-links between chains make a polymer more rigid.

blocks.text: A polymer is built from many small units joined in a chain. This section covers what a polymer is made of and how it is written.

items.meaning: A substance with very large molecules, made of many small repeating units.

The atoms in the chain are joined to other atoms by strong **covalent bonds**.

blocks.text: Polymers differ from small molecules because their chains are so long. This section covers the forces within and between the chains.

rows: Weaker than covalent bonds, but relatively strong compared with small molecules

blocks.text: Some polymers have covalent bonds between their chains, called cross-links. This section covers what that does to the properties.

rows: Chains can slide over each other

blocks.text: A polymer with cross-links, such as melamine, does not melt when heated. Too much energy is needed to overcome the cross-links.

items: A plastic bag polymer stretches because it has weak intermolecular forces.
A plastic bottle polymer is more rigid, stronger and has a higher melting point.
Polymers are poor conductors of electricity, so they are used to coat wires.

checks.q: What type of bond joins the atoms in a polymer chain?
Explain why poly(ethene) is a solid at room temperature but methane is a gas.
checks.a: Poly(ethene) has much larger molecules, so stronger intermolecular forces. More energy is needed to overcome them, so its melting point is higher.

checks.q: Explain why polymers without cross-links can stretch more than polymers with cross-links.
checks.a: The chains can slide over each other, because the intermolecular forces holding them are weaker than cross-links.

worked_example.question: Methane is a gas at room temperature but poly(ethene) is a solid at room temperature. Explain why methane and poly(ethene) exist in different states at room temperature.
answer_points: Methane has much smaller molecules, so it has weaker intermolecular forces.
The intermolecular forces need less energy to overcome.
So the boiling and melting point is lower and methane is a gas.
Or: poly(ethene) has much larger molecules, so stronger intermolecular forces that need more energy to break, so its melting and boiling point is higher and it is a solid.
worked_example.tip: Write about either methane or poly(ethene), in four linked steps. Do not refer to weaker covalent bonds or to breaking covalent bonds.

worked_example.question: Four different substances are described. Substance 1: melting point 1085 °C, shiny solid, conducts electricity. Substance 2: melting point 770 °C, white crystals, conducts electricity when dissolved in water. Substance 3: melting point 120 °C, flexible solid, does not conduct electricity. Substance 4: melting point 78 °C, white crystals, does not conduct electricity. Which of the substances is a polymer? Explain your answer.
answer_points: Polymers have low melting points, and substance 3 has a low melting point.
Polymers do not conduct electricity, and substance 3 does not conduct electricity.
Polymers can be flexible, and substance 3 is flexible.
worked_example.tip: One mark for substance 3, then any two reasons. Choosing substance 1 or 2 scores zero, and substance 4 earns at most one mark.
